title: contextual-heuristics-filer-and-ephemeral-remedier
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Adds a lightweight on-call brief generator and a sandboxed, read-only remediation runner. No end-user API changes.
body:
Summary: Introduces two small, focused incident-response utilities inside incident-bot: a heuristics filer that ingests alert metadata and emits a 3-line on-call brief (mini-brief) prioritizing what to check first, and an ephemeral (sandboxed) remedier that can run read-only diagnostics and gated remediation suggestions in a safe environment. The intent is to reduce mean-time-to-first-action for oncall engineers and to provide a low-risk way to fast-run repeatable diagnostics during early investigation.

Motivation and context: On recent pager storms we observed that responders spend disproportionately long time finding the initial quick signal to validate whether a service is degraded vs an upstream problem (ENG-1284). Existing runbooks are often long and require manual scanning. We want a very small single-screen brief that highlights the top 3 heuristics and provides an immediately-runnable, read-only diagnostic harness that collects targeted artifacts (top traces, recent error counts, key metrics sample). This PR implements the core pieces used by our SRE rotation pilots.

What this change does:
- Adds heuristics-filer: a rule engine that maps alert labels, service ownership, SLO hit types, and recent deploy markers to a ranked list of three investigative heuristics (e.g., "check async queue depth", "validate upstream 3rd-party OK", "confirm KV cache hit-rate"). Each heuristic includes the rationale and one-line command suggestion.
- Adds ephemeral-remedier: a sandbox runner that executes a set of safe, read-only diagnostic commands (metrics snapshot, trace tail, log grep with size bounds) in an ephemeral container and returns an attachable bundle link. It is explicitly disabled for any remediation actions that mutate state; remediation suggestions are produced as plain-text guidance that require explicit confirmation via a separate secured workflow.
- Wire up a lightweight /oncall/mini-brief endpoint consumed by the web UI and Slack helper. The endpoint returns the mini-brief + a single ephemeral bundle URL when requested.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked in Linear (ENG-1284) [x] unit tests for rule scoring [x] integration tests for sandbox runner [x] basic UI integration (Slack button) [x] docs snippet in README / runbook snippets [ ] add SLO-based tuning (follow-up).

High level commits: 1) heuristics engine + test vectors; 2) ephemeral runner scaffold + sandbox container config; 3) integration adapter for alert payloads and Slack action; 4) docs and runbook examples; 5) fixer commit for CI flaky test.

Changed files (high-level):
- src/heuristics/filer.py - core rule engine and scorer
- src/heuristics/tests/test_filer.py - unit tests and edge cases
- src/ephemeral/runner.py - sandbox runner implementation and constraints
- src/ephemeral/sandbox/Dockerfile - minimal readonly image used in CI and staging
- integrations/slack/mini_brief_adapter.py - small adapter for Slack actions
- docs/oncall/mini-briefs.md - runbook + example queries
- ci/flake-fixes.yml - test timeout tuning to reduce false negatives
- pkg/ephemeral/README.md - operational notes and security model

Review conversation (high level):
- Marco Reyes (reviewer): "Nice focused surface area. A couple of questions: how do we prevent sensitive logs from leaking in the ephemeral bundles? Can the sandbox inadvertently escalate permissions?"
- Aisha (author): "Sandbox image is strictly read-only, runs under an unprivileged user and the collector has a whitelist of keys and size limits. I added pkg/ephemeral/README.md describing the guarantees. We also scrub PII from logs using the log-scrubber plugin before bundle upload."
- Priya Patel (reviewer): "Rule engine looks good but scoring feels too static. Suggest adding a small decay factor for deploy markers so that an older deploy doesn't dominate heuristics."
- Aisha: "Added a decay param and unit tests (test_filer decay cases). The decay is configurable via env so ops can tune per-service."
- Jonah Li (reviewer): "CI flake on the sandbox integration; re-run fixed it. Also requested clearer error surface when bundle upload fails."
- Aisha: "Added clearer error messages and retry logic for bundle upload. CI green after fix. See final commit message 'retry: clearer bundle upload error and timeout'."

CI summary: initial run failed due to a timeout in sandbox integration (test_ephemeral_integration). Timeout increased and test hardened in commit 5. Subsequent runs: build ✓, unit tests ✓, integration tests ✓, lint ✓, e2e flaky test retried once then passed. Overall status: pass.

Security and operational notes:
- Sandbox runs in a restricted namespace; network egress to external endpoints is blocked except to our artifact store.
- Bundle URLs expire after 24 hours and are signed with short-lived tokens.
- Audit events are emitted for all ephemeral runs (user, alert_id, heuristics chosen).
- No write actions are enabled by default; remediation suggestions are post-facto guidance that require a separate, audited workflow to execute.

Backwards compatibility and breaking changes: No public API changes to the alert payload schema. The new /oncall/mini-brief endpoint is additive. Breaking change: false.

Merge and rollout: Merged via squash-merge on 2026-02-15 after approvals from Marco and Priya. Feature gated behind a config flag INCIDENT_MINIBRIEF_ENABLED=false by default. Rollout plan: enable for SRE rotation cohort canary group first-week, monitor usage, then widen.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- Add SLO-aware heuristics tuning (ENG-1302).
- Add signed printable one-pager for pagers on-call training.
- Add ability to attach user-provided safe scripts under a strict curations list.

Notes for reviewers: please see docs/oncall/mini-briefs.md for example payloads and sample heuristics. If any team wants early access to the canary, ping the SRE rotation list.
